newsitem.title: USA: Media/telecom issuers return to US junk corp mart.
newsitem.headline: Media/telecom issuers return to US junk corp mart.

text.p: Renewed price stability and investor optimism in the high yield market is prompting a resurgence of larger, more aggressive deals from media and telecommunications issuers, syndicate officials said.
Two offerings that had been postponed due to poor market conditions several weeks ago have reappeared on the forward calendar, they noted.
The deals are a $900 million 144a senior note offering from Comcast Cellular, a unit of Comcast Inc, and a $75 million 144a senior subordinated note offering from Radio One Inc.
Both are expected to be priced in the next several weeks.
Market sources said Comcast Cellular has shortened the maturity of the debt to 10 years from 12 years. Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette will be the lead underwriter for the deal.
Comcast officials could not be reached for comment.
In another sign of improved market conditions, Allied Waste Industries is expected to offer $240 million in 10-year zero coupon bonds later this week, market sources said.
An Allied Waste spokesman declined to comment.
Proceeds will be used to refinance debt and warrants issued to Laidlaw Inc in connection with Allied Waste's purchase of Laidlaw's solid waste operations last year, the sources said.
Analysts said investor appetite for interest-rate-sensitive zero coupon bonds may have returned along with the recent strength in the Treasury market.
Market sources said GST Telecom Inc, a local exchange carrier, will offer $230 million in 10-year senior secured notes via Morgan Stanley & Co next week.
The deal has a three-year prefunded structure, meaning proceeds from the offering will be set aside to pay the coupon on the bonds for a three-year period.
Calls to GST officials were not returned.

In the investment-grade market, CSX Corp restructured its upcoming $2.05 billion debt offering, replacing a 30-year capital securities tranche with a $350 million tranche of 30-year debt with an eight-year put, market sources said.
CSX and Salomon Brothers, the lead underwriter of the offering, declined to comment.
The deal is expected to be priced as soon as Wednesday afternoon, market sources said.
Earlier this morning, Telex Communications Inc priced $125 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes to yield 10.50 percent via Chase Securities Inc.
Proceeds from the high-yield offering will be used to finance a leveraged buyout of the company as well as to refinance $100 million in outstanding Telex 12 percent senior notes due 2004.
